candidate.answerReason: Completing the square identifies two opposite 90-degree sectors of a radius-4 disk. Their total area is 8π, approximately 25.13.

methods.label: Reveal the disk and its sectors
methods.explanation:
Completing the square makes the geometry of the inequalities visible:
\[
f(t)=(t+3)^2-8.
\]
Set \(u=x+3\) and \(v=y+3\). This translates the region, preserving its area. The two conditions become
\[
u^2+v^2\le16,
\qquad u^2\le v^2.
\]
The first condition describes the disk of radius \(4\) centered at the origin. The second is equivalent to \(|u|\le|v|\), so it selects the wedge above both lines \(v=u\) and \(v=-u\), together with the wedge below both lines.

These boundary lines have slopes \(1\) and \(-1\), so they are perpendicular. The selected parts of the disk are therefore two opposite \(90^\circ\) sectors. All boundary points are included because the inequalities are weak, and the two sectors meet only at the origin.

Their total area is
\[
2\left(\frac{90}{360}\pi\cdot4^2\right)
=8\pi\approx25.13.
\]
The closest choice is \(\boxed{25\text{, choice E}}\).
methods.levelReason: Completing the square, translating coordinates, recognizing perpendicular lines, and computing sector areas are all within high-school geometry and algebra.
